baku.headline: Stone lanes, an open sea
baku.intro: Start inside the walls of Icherisheher, then follow the boulevard out to the Caspian. Save a clear day for Gobustan and the fire peninsula.
baku.finish: The Caspian shoreline and a nonstop schedule are the draw. Leave room for wind, an evening arrival and a driver on the excursion day.

tbilisi.headline: Warm water under a cold sky
tbilisi.intro: Cross the river between old balconies and the domes of Abanotubani. Use the city as a base for Mtskheta and, if the weather holds, Kakheti.
tbilisi.finish: Choose the Old Town for time on foot or Station Square for a different starting point. Keep the countryside days flexible if the roads turn wintry.

budapest.headline: Both sides of the river
budapest.intro: Take the river in at dusk. Spend daylight in the market hall, under the steam at the baths, or across the bridge on the Buda hills.
budapest.finish: Pest puts the Opera and central sights close together. The Buda stay offers space and parking, with more of the eastern city reached by transit.

vienna.headline: The city after the lights come on
vienna.intro: Pair the museums and palaces with winter markets after dark. Plan by U-Bahn or tram and leave time to get warm between stops.
vienna.finish: Pick Vienna for galleries, palaces and winter markets. Compare the rail and U-Bahn connections carefully and keep an eye on the higher lodging estimate.

prague.headline: Five nights across the river
prague.intro: Start under the spires of the Old Town, cross the Vltava for castle views, then give one day to Kutná Hora by train.
prague.finish: Prague is the shorter option. A confirmed metro connection makes the Žižkov and Vinohrady side of the city easier to plan from.
